title: Edit Note text
lede: A Click on an idle Note starts **Editing**, with the caret where it landed; a new Note opens in Editing. While Editing the body is a real textarea laid out exactly like the idle text, so a press there only Raises and Drags start from the Grip strip and handles alone. Editing ends on Escape, a press on empty Board, or a press on another Note.

files.question: What does a press on this Note do, idle and while Editing?
files.summary: Renders the idle text or the textarea, turns a Click into `startEditing` with a measured caret, and ends Editing elsewhere when pressed.
files.owns: The textarea, caret placement on focus, Escape, and ending another Note's Editing on press.
files.never: Decides Click versus Drag: the controller does.

files.question: Which text offset is under the Click?
files.summary: `caretPositionFromPoint` on the idle text, or `null` (end of text) when it's missing or misses the text.
files.owns: The single DOM call that maps a point to an offset.
files.tested: The scenario 2 browser test, in Chromium and Firefox.

files.question: How does Editing end?
files.summary: Blurs the edited textarea explicitly, then dispatches `stopEditing`.
files.owns: The one way the Board and Notes end Editing.
files.tested: Browser tests for empty Board, another Note and its handle.

files.question: What does a press on empty Board do?
files.owns: Presses and double-clicks on empty Board.
files.tested: Browser test: a press on empty Board ends Editing.

files.question: Which Note is being edited?
files.summary: `startEditing` replaces any other, `stopEditing` clears it; a no-op keeps the state.
files.owns: At most one Note in Editing.

files.question: Which Notes re-render when Editing changes?
files.summary: `useIsEditing(id)` selects a boolean, so only the two Notes whose answer flips re-render.
files.never: Returns a new object from a selector.

files.question: How is typed text saved?
files.summary: `setText` keeps the text exactly as typed and keeps every other Note by reference.
files.tested: Node tests and a profiler browser test.

files.question: What happens on create?
files.summary: `createNote` creates the Note, then starts Editing it.
files.tested: Node test, and the scenario 5 browser test.

files.question: Why doesn't the Escape that cancels a Drag also end Editing?
files.summary: Its window `keydown` listener prevents Escape's default during a Drag; the textarea ignores a prevented Escape.
files.owns: DOM listeners for a Drag session.
files.tested: Browser test: Escape during a strip Drag.

files.question: When is a press a Click?
files.summary: Unchanged: a real release inside the Dead zone calls `io.click`, last.

scenarios.name: A Click on an idle Note starts Editing

steps.title: pointerdown on the idle body
steps.explain: Nobody else is being edited, so `stopEditing` is a no-op that notifies nobody. The body isn't text yet, so `start` captures the pointer and the controller begins a session.

steps.title: pointerup inside the Dead zone: a Click
steps.explain: The controller reports the Click last, after letting go of the pointer. The offset is measured on the idle text, which is still in the DOM, before the store changes.

steps.title: The Note re-renders as a textarea and focuses before paint
steps.explain: Only this Note's `useIsEditing` answer flipped. A layout effect focuses and places the caret before the first frame, so there's no flash at the end of the text. The textarea composes `.text`, so the text doesn't shift (tested by comparing rects and computed styles).

steps.title: Typing
steps.explain: Each change dispatches `setText`, which keeps the text exactly as typed. Only this Note's object is replaced.

scenarios.name: While Editing: a strip Drag, and an Escape that cancels it

steps.title: pointerdown in the textarea
steps.explain: `isInText` sees the textarea: the press only Raises, with no `preventDefault` and no capture, so selecting by dragging and double-clicking a word work natively.

steps.title: pointerdown on the Grip strip
steps.explain: Not text, so `preventDefault` stops focus from moving: the textarea keeps focus and caret while the Note moves.

run.from: // No focus change, no text selection and no native drag.

steps.title: Escape mid-Drag
steps.explain: The window capture listener runs first and prevents Escape's default; the textarea's handler then sees `defaultPrevented` and keeps Editing. Without it one Escape would both cancel the Drag and end Editing.

steps.title: pointerdown on empty Board, or on another Note or its handle
steps.explain: Both go through `useStopEditing`, which blurs explicitly: the other Note's press calls `preventDefault`, so focus would otherwise stay put until the textarea unmounted.

run.from: // A press on another Note, handles included, ends Editing wherever it is.

steps.title: Nothing to end
steps.explain: With no Note in Editing, `withEditing` returns the same state, so the store notifies nobody and nothing re-renders.

scenarios.name: A new Note opens in Editing

steps.title: Double-click on empty Board
steps.explain: `createNote` creates, then starts Editing; the Note mounts with no pending caret, so the layout effect puts it at the end of the (empty) text.

notes.title: The toolbar doesn't re-render on Editing yet
notes.detail: The spec expects the toolbar among the re-renders, but nothing in it reads Editing until the colour and delete issues. The profiler test checks only Notes.

notes.title: Caret measured on the idle text
notes.detail: The offset comes from the div before the textarea replaces it; this relies on both laying out identically, which the no-shift test guards. Counter-argument: a long Note that scrolls inside the textarea would measure differently, but idle text never scrolls.

notes.title: Any press on another Note ends Editing
notes.detail: Including a right-button press, which isn't a Press. Simpler, and harmless.
